budgeted_pagination_limit100.baseline_fingerprint_check: The prior benchmark did not retain the literal fingerprint. A fresh limit-10 control from the same unchanged retained database was captured immediately before this run; all limit-100 pages equal that fingerprint.
budgeted_pagination_limit100.method: Only the requested page limit changed; the 20000-byte cap is identical. API pagination uses returned next_offset, checks serialized bytes for every page, ordinal coverage and fingerprint equality. Timings exclude the initial control and two CLI checks; the prior run also included lightweight per-page coverage checks. Sequential runs on a normally cached local machine are not a controlled CPU benchmark. No source, installation, or database edits.

methods.original_baseline: Public create/ingest and one representative record() call per case; remaining equivalently shaped short JSON records inserted directly into scratch databases to bound setup time. Each chunk has three short findings. Full pagination uses the real findings API with limit10 and budget20000; separate real CLI single-page invocations. Counter pass is separate from timings. Original results are preserved unchanged.

supported_runtime_comparison.method: Same retained synthetic 3000-chunk database. Sequential full API pagination, first limit10 then limit100, both budget20000; resume exclusively via returned next_offset. Validate actual compact UTF-8 packet size, complete ordered ordinals, and every page fingerprint against both runs first fingerprint. Real CLI first/last page of both runs use the same Python executable with -B and must equal the API packet. Source records, analysis records and meta revision checked unchanged before/after. Timings exclude initial state checks and CLI checks but include lightweight pagination validations. No writes to repository, installed tools, source text or analysis database.
supported_runtime_comparison.preparation_boundary: Original scratch corpus used public create/ingest, one public record() validation and direct bulk insertion of remaining equivalent short analysis records; it is a synthetic throughput case, not an end-to-end record-write benchmark.
supported_runtime_comparison.measurement_limits: A single sequential pair under normal local OS caching, not isolated cold-I/O or repeated statistical benchmarking; page-count/byte/fingerprint evidence is deterministic, wall times are local observations. Python3.9 historical results remain exploratory and are not the final performance conclusion.

historical_measurements_status: The original environment/cases and budgeted_pagination_limit100 were measured with Python 3.9.6 (outside documented 3.10+ support), retained only as exploratory history. Use supported_runtime_comparison for final conclusions. The historical environment.tool_sha256 hashed normalized read_text content; supported_runtime_comparison.tool_raw_bytes_sha256 hashes original source bytes.
